title: The Legion Hall session with Johnny Wiggs that launched Southland
summary: The Johnny Wiggs session at the Legion Hall got great reviews and put Mares in the record business; he followed with Girard, Delaney and Lewis.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: At the Legion Hall. I thought maybe it was at Lentz or something. No, no, it was across the street from Lentz.
They called it, they had two or three different names. Anyhow, I called it the Legion Hall. And we made that and they have the Johnny Wiggs, which got some real, real good reviews,
especially for Harry Shields and Tom Brown was on that one,
and he got some great reviews, and Johnny Wiggs.
Was it a place where there was music there?

Yes, the Basin Street Six was playing there at that time, and I got the job for Johnny Wiggs and his outfit, and I came over one night and I says, Johnny, I'm going to do a little recording this band. I like it, it sounds good, it's got the old-time sound. In fact, that session put me in the business. I tried to sell it to two or three of the smaller record companies, nobody didn't like it, and I thought, well, something's wrong here. I'm going to have to try this thing myself. I did, and I sent it to a record changer in different spots and downbeat and all, and they thought it was terrific, so that put me in business. I thought I'd go on and make some more of them, which I did. I made the George Girard and the Jack Delaney and the George Lewis. By the way, I recorded George Lewis in the studio. That's something that George didn't have much chance to do.
